newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro bourses climb on healthy Wall St close.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro bourses climb on healthy Wall St close.

text.p: European bourses climbed in early trading on Wednesday after a healthy close on Wall Street as fresh U.S. economic data helped calm inflation jitters.

On currency markets, the dollar was little changed from its levels late on Tuesday but the mark strengthened against its European counterparts as a new bout of nerves set in about prospects for monetary union.

London, Frankfurt and Paris all chalked up early gains after Tuesday's losses, which had been largely prompted by worries about more statistics due on Wednesday and Friday on the state of the powerful U.S. economy.
London's FTSE index gained 0.3 percent as investors set aside some of these fears and drew encouragement from the Dow Jones industrials' close, up 0.6 percent and back above the 6,000-level.

Behind New York's strong close was a smaller-than-expected rise in the third-quarter U.S. wages index, which eased inflation fears and sent interest rates falling to the lowest levels in more than 6-1/2 months.
But some apprehension remained in London ahead of a monetary meeting later in the day between finance minister Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England Governor Eddie George, dealers said.
"The market is not going to go roaring away with so much press and so many concerns about this meeting," said one dealer.

George is expected to push for a rate hike after a report on Tuesday showed an unexpected jump in British consumer borrowing. But many analysts believe Clarke will not agree to this so close to a general election, which must be held by May 1997.

"We believe interest rates ought to be higher. They may not do it today but pressure is mounting and that may cast a shadow over the market," the dealer said. "It's a question of when it happens, not if it happens."

Many European investors remained on the sidelines ahead of U.S. data on third-quarter gross domestic product due at 1330 GMT and housing for September at 1500 GMT. But more important clues on the health of the American economy may appear in U.S. employment statistics on Friday.
The best performer in Europe was Frankfurt, where shares strengthened 0.62 percent, encouraged by firmer German bonds and Wall Street's close.

In Paris, French stocks opened down but quickly climbed into the plus column as investors digested the rebound in New York. Analysts said the short-term trend remained bearish and hostage to Wall Street.

The dollar was steady in early European business, surrendering centre stage to the mark, which climbed against other European currencies amid economic and monetary union (EMU) worries after reports that the European Commission might rule against a French deficit-cutting plan to qualify for EMU.
Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen warned that "fudging" of the strict single currency criteria were "absolutely killing" for German public confidence in EMU.

"At the moment sentiment has turned into the mark's favour, and until we see the next political statements on EMU...I think that momentum is going to stay," said Keith Edmonds, chief analyst at IBJ International in London.
The mark rose to 3.3844 French francs in early deals from late Tuesday's European level of 3.3812. It strengthened to 1,009.03 Italian lire from 1,004.15.

The dollar, whose recent strength against the yen has taken it to 42-month highs, stood at 114.35 versus 114.26 late on Tuesday. Many currency traders were awaiting the next slice of U.S. economic data.
CURRENCIES AT 1015 GMT
The dollar was trading around 1.5110 marks and 114.35 yen versus 1.5100 and 114.26 in late European business on Tuesday.
STOCKS AT 1015 GMT
London's FTSE 100 index was up 15.8 points at 4,009.4.
Germany's DAX index was 17.04 higher at 2,690.66.
In Paris, the CAC 40 index was up 7.70 at 2133.44.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $380.30 an ounce in the morning, compared to London's Tuesday close of $381.50. Silver was at $4.82, down three cents.
